ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle BAC$, and $E$ is a point on $AD$, with $EF \perp BC$ at point $F$. If $\angle C = 35^\circ$ and $\angle DEF = 15^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $EF\perp BC$ and $\angle DEF=15^\circ$, we have $\angle ADB=90^\circ-15^\circ=75^\circ$. \\
Since $\angle C=35^\circ$, it follows that $\angle CAD=75^\circ-35^\circ=40^\circ$. \\
Since $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle BAC$, we have $\angle BAC=2\angle CAD=80^\circ$, hence $\angle B=180^\circ-\angle BAC-\angle C=180^\circ-80^\circ-35^\circ=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with A as the top vertex, B at the lower left, and C at the lower right on the straight base BC. Point D lies on BC between B and C, and segment AD is drawn from A to D. Point E lies on AD, and EF is drawn from E down to point F on BC, with EF perpendicular to BC. The given angles are ∠C = 35° and ∠DEF = 15°. Reasoning: Since ED lies along AD and EF is perpendicular to BC, the angle between AD and BC on the B-side is 90° − 15° = 75°, so ∠ADB = 75°. In triangle ADC, ∠ADB is an exterior angle, so ∠ADB = ∠CAD + ∠C. Therefore ∠CAD = 75° − 35° = 40°. Since AD bisects ∠BAC, ∠BAC = 2 × 40° = 80°. Finally, using the angle sum of triangle ABC, ∠B = 180° − 80° − 35° = 65°.
